epithet: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split
lede: The people of Makkah asked for a sign and were shown the moon in two halves, with the mountain between them. They called it magic. This surah answers with five peoples who did the same — and after each asks: “We have made the Qurʾan easy to remember; is there anyone who will take heed?”

names.name: al-Qamar
names.note: From its first ayah. In the hadith it is called by its opening words, Iqtarabati l-sāʿah: the Prophet ﷺ recited “Qāf” and “Iqtarabati l-sāʿah” in the ʿĪd prayers (Muslim 891).

revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī records agreement that it is Makkan. Muqātil excepted three ayat (54:44–46); al-Qurṭubī mentions this and says it is not sound — and ʿĀʾishah settles it in al-Bukhārī: “‘Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more grievous and more bitter’ was sent down to Muḥammad ﷺ in Makkah, when I was a young girl at play.” The traditional order places the surah thirty-seventh.
revelation.when: Makkah, some five years before the Hijrah — the night the moon was split

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ الْقَمَرِ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّهَا فِي قَوْلِ الْجُمْهُورِ. وَقَالَ مُقَاتِلٌ: إِلَّا ثَلَاثَ آيَاتٍ

setting: Anas relates that the people of Makkah asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to show them a sign, and he showed them the moon split in two. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd was there. “The moon was split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two parts — one part above the mountain and one below it — and he said: ‘Bear witness.’”

They had seen it with their own eyes, at Minā, and could not deny that. So they denied what it meant. The surah records the reply they gave, and that it was the reply they always gave: “If they see a sign they turn away and say: ‘Continuous magic.’”

After that the surah stops arguing. It tells the Prophet ﷺ to turn from them, and puts before them the Day they will come out of the graves like scattered locusts — and then five histories in quick succession, each a few ayat long: the people of Nūḥ, ʿĀd, Thamūd, the people of Lūṭ, and Pharaoh’s. Each ends in the same two beats: “Then how was My punishment, and My warnings?” and “We have made the Qurʾan easy for remembrance; is there anyone who will remember?”

Then it addresses Quraysh directly: are your disbelievers better than those? “Or do they say: we are a host that will prevail? The host will be routed, and they will turn their backs.” When that came down in Makkah the Muslims were a persecuted handful, and ʿUmar is reported to have wondered what host was meant. On the day of Badr the Prophet ﷺ came out of his shelter in his coat of mail, reciting it.

occasions.title: The splitting of the moon
occasions.text: “The people of Makkah asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to show them a sign, so he showed them the moon in two halves, until they saw Ḥirāʾ between them.” Ibn Masʿūd said: “The moon was split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two parts, and the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Bear witness.’”
occasions.source: Anas ibn Mālik: al-Bukhārī (3868) and Muslim (2802). ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: al-Bukhārī (3636) and Muslim (2800).

occasions.title: Recited at Badr
occasions.text: On the day of Badr the Prophet ﷺ was in his tent, saying: “O Allah, I call upon Your covenant and Your promise. O Allah, if You will, You will not be worshipped after today.” Abū Bakr took his hand and said: “Enough, Messenger of Allah; you have pressed your Lord.” He was in his armour, and he went out saying: “The host will be routed, and they will turn their backs.”

occasions.title: On the decree
occasions.text: The idolaters of Quraysh came disputing with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the decree, and there came down: “The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces: ‘Taste the touch of Saqar.’ We have created everything by measure.”

aim: To remind of the signs and the warnings, and to show the fate of those who denied them — which is why it repeats: “We have made the Qurʾan easy for remembrance; is there anyone who will remember?”

outline.title: The sign, and their answer
outline.summary: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. If they see a sign they turn away and say, “Continuous magic.” They denied and followed their desires. So turn from them. The Day the Caller calls to a terrible thing, they will come out of the graves with downcast eyes, like locusts scattered, hastening towards the Caller. The disbelievers will say: “This is a hard day.”

outline.title: The people of Nūḥ
outline.summary: They denied Our servant and said, “A madman.” He called on his Lord: “I am overcome, so help.” We opened the gates of the sky with water pouring, and made the earth burst with springs, and the waters met for a matter already decreed. We carried him on a thing of planks and nails, sailing under Our eyes. We have made the Qurʾan easy for remembrance; is there anyone who will remember?

outline.title: ʿĀd
outline.summary: ʿĀd denied. We sent against them a screaming wind on a day of unrelenting misfortune, plucking people away as though they were the trunks of uprooted palms.

outline.title: Thamūd
outline.summary: Thamūd denied the warnings: “A single mortal from among us — shall we follow him?” We sent the she-camel as a trial for them, and the water was to be shared. They called their companion, and he took a sword and hamstrung her. We sent upon them a single blast, and they became like the dry twigs of a pen-builder.

outline.title: The people of Lūṭ, and Pharaoh
outline.summary: The people of Lūṭ denied the warnings. We sent a storm of stones upon them, except the family of Lūṭ, whom We saved before dawn. They had even demanded his guests of him, so We blinded their eyes. And the warnings came to the people of Pharaoh: they denied all Our signs, and We seized them with the seizing of One Mighty, Omnipotent.

outline.title: And you?
outline.summary: Are your disbelievers better than those, or have you an immunity in the scriptures? Or do they say, “We are a host that will prevail”? The host will be routed, and they will turn their backs. No — the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more grievous and more bitter. We have created everything by measure; and Our command is but one, like the blink of an eye. Everything they did is in the records. The mindful will be among gardens and rivers, in a seat of truth, near a Sovereign, Omnipotent.

keyAyah.why: The refrain, said four times. The Qurʾan is not hard to take a lesson from; the only question is whether anyone will.

virtues.text: “The moon was split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two parts, one part above the mountain and one part below it. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ‘Bear witness.’”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the prayers of al-Aḍḥā and al-Fiṭr “Qāf, by the glorious Qurʾan” and “The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split.”

before: Al-Najm ended: the Approaching has drawn near. Al-Qamar opens: the Hour has drawn near — and gives the sign.
after: Al-Qamar closes with the mindful “near a Sovereign, Omnipotent.” Al-Raḥmān opens with the name of that Sovereign’s mercy, and with a refrain of its own: which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?
